subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native Windows PowerShell smoke lane include both `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or should the first lane start narrower with only already-proven commands?
rationale: The request fits OpenClaw's test-infrastructure direction, but the exact recurring Windows command set and runner cost require maintainer intent before the open PR can be treated as the right fix.

options.title: Prove full smoke before merge
options.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after both commands pass in the Windows `pwsh` lane with redacted proof.

options.title: Start with narrower coverage
options.body: Land only the native PowerShell commands that already pass, then track `build:strict-smoke` as follow-up once it is Windows-safe.

options.title: Defer recurring Windows smoke
options.body: Keep the issue open but pause the PR until Windows runner budget and build-smoke ownership are settled.

recommendation.title: Prove full smoke before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after both commands pass in the Windows `pwsh` lane with redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow changes and adjacent PowerShell-safe docs tooling.
